project_identity: IESO Nova Scotia fast-acting generation procurement
known_buying_event: Fast-acting natural gas capacity to support system reliability and transition from coal.

evidence_sources.source_quote:
### Fast-Acting Electricity Generation

IESO Nova Scotia has initiated its first procurement process, seeking to secure at least 300 megawatts of reliable natural gas generation capacity for the province.

While it might seem surprising to start with natural gas when moving to a cleaner electricity system, it is the necessary next step in the plan to achieve Nova Scotia’s 80% renewables goal.

Having a flexible and dependable resource like natural gas provides a critical foundation of electricity that enables the new system to deliver a reliable supply of power to Nova Scotians, even in extended cold snaps or periods where wind isn’t sufficient to meet the province’s demand.

Importantly, these new facilities are not designed to run all the time, but instead to generate electricity quickly when we need them — and power down when we don’t. These facilities will also have the ability to switch to non-fossil fuels, such as hydrogen or biodiesel, when they become economically available. They will play a critical role, alongside batteries and other technologies, to provide Nova Scotia with a reliable system in the most cost-effective way.

Nova Scotia needs between 300 and 600 megawatts of fast-acting natural gas-fired generation capacity added to our system to enable the province to continue to meet growing electricity demand, transition away from coal, significantly reduce greenhouse gas emissions, and achieve our renewable energy goals. This need has been identified in the Government of Nova Scotia’s Clean Power Plan and the province’s most recent Integrated Resource Plan completed by Nova Scotia Power.

**On July 10, 2026, IESO Nova Scotia launched a competitive procurement, issuing a Request for Proposals (RFP) for one or two 300-megawatt fast-acting natural gas electricity generation facilities for the province.**

Draft versions of the procurement documents were posted in March 2026 for stakeholder review and feedback, which has informed numerous updates and clarifications in the final documents below. An overview of feedback from industry, regulatory, and community stakeholders, as well as IESO Nova Scotia’s responses, is available [here](https://www.ieso-ns.ca/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/IESO-Nova-Scotia-Stakeholder-Feedback-Overview-300-MW-RFP-launch-July-10-2026.pdf), and a summary of the updates made to the RFP document can be found [here](https://www.ieso-ns.ca/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/IESO-Nova-Scotia-BG-300-MW-RFP-launch-July-10-2026-1.pdf).

We look forward to receiving competitive bids from proponents.

**Update — September 11, 2026:**

The timeline for submissions for the fast-acting generation procurement process is being extended, with proposals now due by January 21, 2027, in response to  proponents’ request for additional time to develop their most competitive proposals possible. New procurement documents relating to this extension, including an evaluated project cost model, an RFP addendum, and a revised proposal information and workbook form, have been added below.

1. [Fast-Acting Generation Request for Proposals](https://www.ieso-ns.ca/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/Fast-Acting-Generation-Request-for-Proposals.pdf)
2. [Fast-Acting Generation Tolling Agreement](https://www.ieso-ns.ca/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/Fast-Acting-Generation-Tolling-Agreement.pdf)
3. [Fast-Acting Generation Form of Lease](https://www.ieso-ns.ca/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/Fast-Acting-Generation-Form-of-Lease.pdf)
4. [Fast-Acting Generation Registration Form](https://www.ieso-ns.ca/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/Fast-Acting-Generation-Registration-Form.pdf)

7. [Fast-Acting Generation Evaluated Project Cost Model R1](https://www.ieso-ns.ca/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/Fast-Acting-Generation-Evaluated-Project-Cost-Model-R1.xlsx)
8. [Addendum #1](https://www.ieso-ns.ca/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/Fast-Acting-Generation-Addendum-1.pdf)

Addendum No. 1
Dated September 11, 2026

# Fast-Acting Power Generation Procurement Request for Proposals

In accordance with Section 3.3 of the Request for Proposals, the Request for Proposals is 
amended as follows.  No other terms of the Request for Proposals are amended or waived 
by this addendum.

All capitalized terms in this Addendum have the meanings ascribed to them in the Request 
for Proposals or Tolling Agreement unless otherwise defined herein.

1. Section 2.1 d) Projects (ii) RFP is amended as follows:

Please delete the paragraph in the RFP and replace it with the text below.

*“The Facility will use proven Prime Mover technology with the same Prime Mover 
model series used at the Facility having been deployed for a minimum of five years 
in at least three (3) power generation facilities that have: i) reached commercial 
operation prior to January 1, 2021; and ii) have individually been operated for a 
minimum of 10,000 fired hours.  For greater clarity, new models which are minor 
variations and new versions or model variations of proven model series and 
products are considered acceptable.”*

Page **1** of **5**

---

2. Section 3.1 RFP is amended as follows:

Please delete the table in the RFP and replace it with the table below.

| Milestone | Date |
| --- | --- |
| IESO Nova Scotia release of the RFP and Tolling Agreement | July 10, 2026 (the “RFP Effective Date”) |
| Proponent’s deadline for submitting a completed Registration Form and Proposal Package Fee | August 21, 2026 (the “RFP Registration Deadline”) |
| Proponent’s deadline for submitting questions and comments, if any | November 13, 2026 (the “Question and Comment Deadline”) |
| IESO Nova Scotia’s deadline for issuing Addenda to the RFP and Tolling Agreement, if any | December 15, 2026 |
| Proposal submission deadline | January 21, 2027 at 3:00 PM (AST) (the “Proposal Submission Deadline”) |
| Target Date for notification of Selected Proponents | May 12, 2027 |

3. Section 5.10 RFP is amended by adding the following paragraph at the end of the 
Section:

*“Each Proponent acknowledges and agrees that the IRP Optimization Model used 
in the assessment of Proposals in accordance with Section 4.4(d) and IESO Nova* 
*Scotia’s selection in its Discretion of one, two or no Proposed Projects in 
accordance with Section 4.5 may, in each case, be informed by information 
received by IESO Nova Scotia through requests for qualifications, requests for 
information, requests for proposals and/or other processes which may be 
undertaken by IESO Nova Scotia from time to time, including, without limitation, in 
connection with requests for qualifications, requests for information and requests 
for proposals and other processes intended to assess the potential deployment of 
alternative technologies.”*

Page **2** of **5**

---

4. RFP Appendix G – 2026 Integrated Resource Plan is amended by adding the 
following sentence to the end of the first paragraph thereof:

*“An IRP may be informed by, amongst other things, information received by IESO* 
*Nova Scotia through requests for qualifications, requests for information, requests 
for proposals and/or other processes which may be undertaken by IESO Nova* 
*Scotia from time to time, to the extent such information may be publicly 
disclosed.”*

5. Appendix B – Tolling Agreement, Section 2.2(d) is amended by adding the following 
sentence to the paragraph:

*“The annual requirement to fulfill the Community Benefits Obligations shall 
commence on the Effective Date.”*

6. Appendix B – Tolling Agreement, Exhibit T – Functional Specifications are amended 
by adding the following sentence to Section 4. Electrical and Interconnection
Requirements, part (d):

*“Transmission System Interconnection Requirements (TSIR) Section 7.5.4 Inertia* 
*Constant is currently under review. For the purposes of this Facility, there shall be
no minimum inertia constant of the combined prime mover plus generator unit (H).”*

7. Evaluated Project Cost Model has been updated to update cells E32 and E44 on the 
Heat_Rate worksheet, so the text labels match the correct federal cost of carbon as 
already included in calculation cells F32 and F44.  Proponents are requested to 
refer to the updated version (Fast-Acting Generation Evaluated Project Cost Model 
R1) that will be posted to the website.

Page **3** of **5**

---

8. Proposal Information and Workbook Form has been updated in Exhibit C-2 to add a 
section to “ Describe how the Proposed Project will have a pathway to future 
operations without fossil fuels,….” to match Exhibit C-1.    The updated form version
(Fast-Acting Generation Proposal Information & Workbook Form v2.1) that will be 
posted to the website.

9. Appendix B – Tolling Agreement, Exhibit T – Functional Specifications are deleted 
and replaced by the following sentences in Section 2. FACILITY CONFIGURATION 
AND PERFORMANCE REQUIREMENTS, parts (i) and (j):

*“i. The Facility shall be capable of achieving MCC from a cold start within ten (10) 
minutes.*

*j. The Facility shall be capable of continuous stable operation at or below twenty 
percent (20%) of MCC.”*

10. Appendix B – Tolling Agreement, Exhibit T – Functional Specifications are deleted 
and replaced by the following sentence in Section 11. PERFORMANCE TESTING, 
part (b):

*“b. The Facility shall demonstrate cold start capability of achieving MCC within ten 
(10) minutes measured from the issuance of a start command to the Facility.*

11. Appendix B – Tolling Agreement, Exhibit F – Fuel Management Protocol are deleted 
and replaced by the following sentence in Section 1.3 (b):

*“b. the Generator shall maintain the dual Fuel capacity of the Facility in accordance 
with Section 2.2(d) of this Agreement;”*

Page **4** of **5**

---

12. Appendix B – Tolling Agreement, Exhibit T – Functional Specifications are deleted 
and replaced by the following sentences in Section 11. PERFORMANCE TESTING, 
parts (a), (d), (e), (f), and (g):

*“a. The Facility shall demonstrate compliance with the MCC.*

*d. The Facility shall demonstrate the MCC for a period of twelve (12) hours on 
natural gas.*

*e. The Facility shall demonstrate the MCC for a period of twelve (12) hours on liquid 
fuel.*

*f. The Facility shall demonstrate the contractual heat rate during the twelve (12) 
hour performance tests.*

g. *Upon request from IESO Nova Scotia the Facility shall demonstrate reliability with
